data.reasoning: The PKGBUILD and metadata files contain standard, non-malicious packaging logic for building shader-slang. The apparent disagreement is solely due to a transient API error in one model when auditing a LICENSE file, not a genuine security dispute. All models that successfully evaluated the PKGBUILD found no malicious injections or unsafe patterns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The 'inconclusive' verdict from qwen was triggered by an HTTP 400 API error while processing a LICENSE file, despite its own PKGBUILD assessment being 'safe'. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and returned 'safe'. The openrouter report (advisory) also returned 'safe'. There is no actual security disagreement.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit one LICENSE file due to an HTTP 400 API error, causing its overall package verdict to be inconclusive.
learnings: Transient API errors on non-executable files (like LICENSE) should not force the entire package verdict to INCONCLUSIVE if all critical executable files (PKGBUILD, .install) are successfully audited and found safe. The tool should decouple file-level API failures from the final package verdict or implement automatic retries for failed file audits.
